title: LLM × Gaokao Admissions
titleZh: LLM × 高考志愿填报：可信升学决策研究
subtitle: Evidence-grounded university choice and application-risk auditing
type: Market research + proposed algorithm/backend/frontend/API architecture (MVP not built)
summary: A rigorous landscape of China’s AI Gaokao volunteer-filling services and adjacent Product Hunt / Hacker News products, with independently sourced limitations, user signals and a focused MVP hypothesis.
summaryZh: 系统研究官方高考志愿服务、夸克/千问、优志愿、掌上高考及海外 AI 升学顾问，明确真实用户信号、数据风险、商业竞争与可验证 MVP 机会。
problem: Applicants and families receive conflicting AI university recommendations but lack a reliable way to verify yearly program eligibility, data provenance and risk.
thesis: Instead of another free AI university recommender, validate a source-grounded draft-application audit and family decision workspace, scoped to one province and one admission batch.
findings: Official and major-platform no-fee advisory products already cover common school search and recommendation flows, raising the bar for a new standalone recommender.
Media tests surfaced inconsistent risk tiers across AI tools and material errors against published admissions data.
Product Hunt tools suggest effective onboarding and longitudinal decision UX; foreign application-probability logic does not transfer directly to China's admission rules.
The proposed initial wedge is checking an existing draft against versioned official data, with LLM used for explanations rather than hard eligibility decisions.
risks: Desk research only: no primary user interviews, independent paid conversion evidence or live admissions algorithm benchmark
Official year-specific data accessibility, licensing and completeness must be verified before launching recommendations
Model hallucinations and admissions-rule mistakes can lead to consequential user harm; testing is mandatory
Seasonal demand and strong free competitors complicate distribution and willingness-to-pay validation
method: Public-source desk research as of 2026-11-09 across Product Hunt, Hacker News, Reddit, App Store, official education authorities, media tests and academic research; facts, voices, vendor claims and hypotheses are explicitly separated.
